name: HA-2600 / HA-2602 / HA-2605 and HA-2620 / HA-2622 / HA-2625
type: Bipolar high-input-impedance singles, compensated or not
tagline: Harris 500 MΩ bipolar singles: HA-2600/2605 (12 MHz, 7 V/µs) and uncompensated HA-2620/2625 (100 MHz, 35 V/µs, gain >5).

lineage.note: Harris-era three-grade datasheets survive on mirrors; macromodels dated Rev 8-01-91 (DW Riemer), library © 1990/1991.
Reissued as FN2902 (HA-2600) and FN2903 (HA-2620/2625, rev .6 June 2003); HA-2602 moved to /883 sheet.
Hosts HA-2600 and HA-2620 product pages and HA-2600, HA-2602/883, HA-2620 datasheets.

Bipolar, 500 MΩ input (300 MΩ lower grades, model)

reputation.summary: No hi-fi praise has been verified. These Harris parts were reportedly cited in late-1970s/1980s Walt Jung-era audio literature as high-slew, high-impedance options; modern enthusiast praise is minimal. Treat this as a historical entry until the Jung citations are confirmed.
typical_uses: High-slew line and instrumentation stages (reportedly, SID era)
Fast high-gain stages from high-impedance sources (HA-2620/2625, gain >5)
caveats: HA-2620/2622/2625 are uncompensated, stable only at gain >5: never use as followers or low-gain stages.
HA3-2625-5 is obsolete; other codes likely only from surplus, new-old stock or Rochester Electronics.
Grade values come from EWB/MicroSim models; a measured HA2-2600-8 sample: 12.4 MHz, +7.5/−6.4 V/µs, 0.85 mV, CMRR 107 dB.
Noise, THD, supply current and supply range are unverified.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found (none searched). Supply is surplus, new-old stock or Rochester Electronics. Check Harris/Intersil-era logos and date codes. Slew (~7 vs ~35 V/µs) and follower stability tell the dies apart: a 2620/2625 oscillates as a follower.
alternatives: OPA1611 / OPA1612 (modern low-noise bipolar; editorial pick)
LT1363 / LT1361 (fast voltage-feedback bipolar; editorial pick)

claims_confirmed: Renesas hosts the HA-2600 product page and datasheet (https://www.renesas.com/en/products/ha-2600, https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/ha-2600-datasheet).
Renesas HA-2600 copy has PDF metadata dated 16 Jan 2006 (https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/ha-2600-datasheet).
HA-2600: 12 MHz, 7 V/µs, 150 kV/V, 500 MΩ, internally compensated (https://www.renesas.com/en/products/ha-2600).
HA-2602/883 has its own datasheet: 12 MHz, 500 MΩ, 1 nA, 0.5 mV, 150 kV/V (https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/ha-2602883-datasheet).
HA-2620: 100 MHz GBW, stable at gain >5, 35 V/µs, 150 kV/V, 500 MΩ (https://www.renesas.com/en/products/ha-2620).
HA-2620, HA-2625 datasheet is Intersil FN2903, rev FN2903.6, June 2003 (https://en.sekorm.com/doc/766115.html).
Harris-era 'HA-2620, HA-2622, HA-2625' datasheet on RS Online (https://docs.rs-online.com/d1f9/0900766b80029c45.pdf).
Harris-era 'HA-2600, HA-2602, HA-2605' datasheet on a mirror (https://www.elektronik.ropla.eu/pdf/stock/hrs/ha-26(00_02_05).pdf).
Rochester Electronics HA-2620, HA-2625 datasheet copy under HA2-2625-5 (https://datasheet.octopart.com/HA2-2625-5-Rochester-Electronics-datasheet-181209774.pdf).
refuted_claims: HA-2620/2625 GBW is not ~40 MHz (EWB fu): the datasheet gives 100 MHz, stable only at gain >5 (https://www.renesas.com/en/products/ha-2620).
Guessed Renesas URLs .../ha-2600-ha-2602-ha-2605-datasheet and .../ha-2620-ha-2622-ha-2625-datasheet do not exist; real ones are .../dst/ha-2600-datasheet, ha-2620-datasheet, ha-2602883-datasheet.
HA-2622 as an Intersil/Renesas product: no Intersil-era document names it; FN2903.6 covers only HA-2620 and HA-2625.
